documents.title: JSS 1 Music — St. Francis Catholic Secondary School First Term (Weeks 1–9)
documents.subject: Music
documents.description: St. Francis Catholic Secondary School Lagos JSS 1 Music First Term Note covering Definition & Sources of Music, Characteristics of Musical Sound (Pitch, Intensity, Timbre, Duration), Elements of Music, Functions of Music in Society, Staff & Solfa Notation, Clefs & Great Stave, Musical Notes & Rests, Time Signatures, and Classification of Musical Instruments (Weeks 1–9).
documents.rawText:
[Page 1]
Week 1: Introduction to Music — Definition, Origin, and Natural & Human Sources of Musical Sound
Music is the art and science of combining vocal or instrumental sounds in a pleasing, organized, and expressive manner using rhythm, melody, and harmony.
The word "Music" is derived from the Greek word "Mousike" (the art of the Nine Muses, goddesses of arts and sciences in Greek mythology). Sources of musical sound include natural sources (birdsong, wind, ocean waves, thunder, human voice) and man-made musical instruments.

1. From which ancient language and mythological root is the English word "Music" derived?
- A) The Greek word "Mousike", referring to the art of the Nine Muses
- B) The Latin word "Sonare", referring to Roman military trumpets
- C) The Hebrew word "Selah", referring to temple cymbals
- D) The Sanskrit word "Raga", referring to seasonal rain chants
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: "Music" originates from the Greek "Mousike", meaning the art presided over by the Muses in Greek mythology.

2. What is the fundamental acoustic difference between "Musical Sound" and "Noise"?
- A) Musical sound is produced by regular, periodic vibrations with definite pitch, whereas noise is produced by irregular, non-periodic vibrations displeasing to the ear
- B) Musical sound travels only through vacuum, whereas noise travels only through solid metals
- C) Musical sound has zero frequency, whereas noise has a fixed harmonic overtone series
- D) Musical sound can only be produced by electronic synthesizers, whereas noise is produced by human voices
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Regular periodic vibrations produce musical tone with definite pitch, while irregular vibrations produce noise.

[Page 3]
Week 2: Characteristics (Properties) of Musical Sound and Elements of Music
Every musical sound possesses four fundamental physical properties: Pitch (height or depth of a sound determined by the frequency of vibration in Hertz), Intensity/Loudness (degree of softness or loudness determined by the amplitude of vibration), Timbre/Quality/Tone Colour (the characteristic quality that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another playing the same pitch, determined by harmonics/overtones), and Duration (length of time a musical sound or silence lasts).
Core elements of music include Rhythm, Melody, Harmony, Dynamics (piano $p$ = soft, forte $f$ = loud, crescendo = gradually louder, diminuendo/decrescendo = gradually softer), Tempo (speed of music: Largo, Adagio, Andante, Moderato, Allegro, Presto), Texture (Monophonic, Homophonic, Polyphonic), and Form (Binary AB, Ternary ABA, Rondo ABACA).

3. If a flute and a violin both play the exact same note Middle C at the exact same loudness for two seconds, which property of musical sound enables a listener to distinguish the flute from the violin?
- A) Timbre (Tone quality or tone colour)
- B) Pitch (Frequency of vibration)
- C) Intensity (Amplitude of vibration)
- D) Duration (Length of note value)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Timbre (tone colour) depends on the harmonic overtones of the instrument and distinguishes different instruments playing the same pitch and loudness.

4. Which physical factor directly determines the Pitch of a musical note?
- A) The frequency (speed) of vibrations per second of the sounding body
- B) The distance between the audience and the concert stage
- C) The colour of the wood used to polish the instrument case
- D) The number of bar lines drawn on the manuscript paper
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Faster vibrations (higher frequency) produce a higher pitch, while slower vibrations (lower frequency) produce a lower pitch.

5. In musical dynamics and tempo terminology, what do the Italian terms "Crescendo" and "Allegro" mean respectively?
- A) Crescendo means gradually getting louder; Allegro means fast, lively, and bright tempo
- B) Crescendo means gradually getting softer; Allegro means very slow and solemn tempo
- C) Crescendo means sudden silence; Allegro means repeating from the beginning
- D) Crescendo means detached staccato notes; Allegro means dying away
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Crescendo ($<$) means gradually becoming louder, and Allegro indicates a fast, lively tempo.

[Page 5]
Week 3: Uses and Impact of Music in Human Society and Nigerian Ceremonies
Music plays vital roles in society: religious worship and liturgy, royal court ceremonies, lullabies (cradle songs to soothe babies to sleep), work songs (to coordinate manual labour and relieve fatigue), war/military martial songs, healing/therapy, education, entertainment, and commercial advertisement/jingles.

6. What type of traditional vocal music is sung softly by mothers or caregivers with gentle rocking rhythms to soothe an infant to sleep?
- A) Lullaby (cradle song)
- B) Dirge (funeral lament)
- C) Panegyric (royal praise chant)
- D) Martial anthem (war song)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A lullaby is a soothing cradle song sung to calm children and help them fall asleep, whereas a dirge is sung at funerals to mourn the dead.

7. Which type of song is performed at a funeral or memorial service to mourn the dead and express grief?
- A) Dirge (Elegy / Lament)
- B) Epithalamium (wedding song)
- C) Carol (festive nativity song)
- D) Serenade (evening courtship song)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A dirge is a somber funeral song lamenting the deceased.

[Page 7]
Week 4: Musical Notation — Tonic Solfa Notation and Staff (Stave) Notation
Musical notation is the system of writing down music using visual symbols so that pitch and rhythm can be read and performed.
Tonic Solfa Notation (developed by Sarah Glover and perfected by Rev. John Curwen) uses seven syllabic note names: doh ($d$), ray ($r$), me ($m$), fah ($f$), soh ($s$), lah ($l$), te ($t$).
Staff (Stave) Notation uses five parallel horizontal lines and four equal spaces counted strictly from the BOTTOM to the TOP (Line 1 is the lowest line; Line 5 is the topmost line).

8. Who perfected the Tonic Solfa notation system ($d, r, m, f, s, l, t$) from Sarah Glover's earlier Norwich sol-fa method in the nineteenth century?
- A) Rev. John Curwen
- B) Guido d'Arezzo
- C) Johann Sebastian Bach
- D) Fela Sowande
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Rev. John Curwen refined and popularized the Tonic Solfa system in England in the 1840s based on Sarah Glover's work.

9. How are the five parallel horizontal lines and four spaces of a standard musical Staff (Stave) numbered?
- A) From the bottom upward (the lowest line is Line 1 and the highest line is Line 5)
- B) From the top downward (the highest line is Line 1 and the lowest line is Line 5)
- C) From the middle line outward in both directions
- D) Randomly depending on the tempo of the song
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Staff lines and spaces are always counted from bottom (1st line/space) to top (5th line/4th space).

[Page 9]
Week 5: Clefs, Letter Names of Lines and Spaces (Treble & Bass Stave), Ledger Lines, and the Great Stave
The first seven letters of the English alphabet ($	ext{A, B, C, D, E, F, G}$) are used as musical pitch names.
The Treble Clef (G Clef) curls around the 2nd line ($	ext{G}$). Its five lines from bottom to top are $	ext{E – G – B – D – F}$ ("Every Good Boy Deserves Favour"), and its four spaces spell $	ext{F – A – C – E}$.
The Bass Clef (F Clef) has two dots straddling the 4th line ($	ext{F}$). Its five lines from bottom to top are $	ext{G – B – D – F – A}$ ("Good Boys Deserve Favour Always"), and its four spaces are $	ext{A – C – E – G}$ ("All Cows Eat Grass").
The Great Stave (Grand Staff) combines the Treble Stave and Bass Stave joined by a brace, with Middle C ($	ext{C}_4$) on a short Ledger Line exactly midway between them.

10. Why is the Treble Clef also known as the "G Clef", and why is the Bass Clef also known as the "F Clef"?
- A) The Treble Clef's inner loop curls around the 2nd line fixing it as note G, while the Bass Clef's two dots sit above and below the 4th line fixing it as note F
- B) The Treble Clef was invented in Germany, while the Bass Clef was invented in France
- C) The Treble Clef is used only for guitars, while the Bass Clef is used only for flutes
- D) The Treble Clef has 7 lines, while the Bass Clef has 6 lines
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The G clef fixes the 2nd line as G above Middle C, and the F clef fixes the 4th line as F below Middle C.

11. Which letter names correspond to the four spaces of the Bass Stave from bottom (Space 1) to top (Space 4)?
- A) A – C – E – G
- B) F – A – C – E
- C) E – G – B – D
- D) G – B – D – F
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The four spaces of the Bass Clef from bottom to top are A, C, E, G ("All Cows Eat Grass"), whereas F, A, C, E are the four spaces of the Treble Clef.

12. What are the short additional lines drawn above or below the five-line staff to accommodate notes that are too high or too low for the staff itself?
- A) Ledger lines
- B) Double bar lines
- C) Slur curves
- D) Fermata lines
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Ledger lines (such as the short line for Middle C between the treble and bass staves) extend the pitch range above or below the staff.

[Page 12]
Week 6: Musical Notes, Rests, Time Values, and Dotted Notes
Musical notes indicate sound duration while rests indicate silence of corresponding duration:
- Breve (Double whole note) = $8$ crotchet beats
- Semibreve (Whole note) = $4$ crotchet beats ($1$ whole note = $2$ minims = $4$ crotchets = $8$ quavers = $16$ semiquavers)
- Minim (Half note) = $2$ crotchet beats
- Crotchet (Quarter note) = $1$ beat
- Quaver (Eighth note, $1$ tail/hook) = $\frac{1}{2}$ beat
- Semiquaver (Sixteenth note, $2$ tails/hooks) = $\frac{1}{4}$ beat
- Demisemiquaver (Thirty-second note, $3$ tails/hooks) = $\frac{1}{8}$ beat.
A dot placed immediately after a note or rest increases its duration by half ($\frac{1}{2}$) of its original value (so a dotted minim $= 2 + 1 = 3$ crotchet beats; a dotted crotchet $= 1 + \frac{1}{2} = 1\frac{1}{2}$ crotchet beats = $3$ quavers).

13. How many semiquavers (sixteenth notes) are equal in total duration to one dotted minim (dotted half note)?
- A) $12$ semiquavers
- B) $8$ semiquavers
- C) $6$ semiquavers
- D) $16$ semiquavers
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A minim equals $2$ crotchets ($8$ semiquavers); the dot adds half its value ($1$ crotchet $= 4$ semiquavers), giving $8 + 4 = 12$ semiquavers ($3$ crotchet beats).

14. How do you visually distinguish a Semibreve Rest from a Minim Rest on the five-line staff?
- A) A Semibreve rest hangs DOWN below the fourth line, whereas a Minim rest sits UP on top of the third line
- B) A Semibreve rest sits on top of the first line, whereas a Minim rest hangs below the fifth line
- C) A Semibreve rest has two hooks to the left, whereas a Minim rest has one hook to the right
- D) A Semibreve rest is shaped like a lightning bolt, whereas a Minim rest is a circle
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The thick rectangular Semibreve rest hangs beneath Line 4 ("heavier $4$-beat rest hangs down"), while the Minim rest sits on top of Line 3.

[Page 14]
Week 7: Dotted Notes, Ties, Slurs, and Accidentals (Sharp, Flat, and Natural Signs)
A tie is a curved line joining two notes of the EXACT SAME pitch so that their durations are added together as a single continuous sound, whereas a slur is a curved line over two or more notes of DIFFERENT pitches indicating that they should be performed smoothly (legato).
Accidentals are signs placed immediately before a note head on the staff to alter its pitch by a semitone:
- A Sharp ($sharp$) raises a note by one semitone (half step).
- A Flat ($ lat$) lowers a note by one semitone (half step).
- A Natural ($
atural$) cancels a previous sharp or flat and restores the note to its original natural pitch.

15. What is the difference between a "Tie" and a "Slur" when both are written as curved lines in staff notation?
- A) A Tie joins two adjacent notes of the exact same pitch into one continuous duration, whereas a Slur connects two or more notes of different pitches to be played smoothly (legato)
- B) A Tie connects notes of different pitches, whereas a Slur joins two notes of the same pitch
- C) A Tie raises a note by a semitone, whereas a Slur lowers a note by a semitone
- D) A Tie marks the end of a composition, whereas a Slur divides the staff into measures
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A tie sustains the sound of two identical pitches across beats or bar lines, whereas a slur indicates smooth, connected phrasing across different pitches.

16. Which accidental symbol cancels a previous Sharp ($sharp$) or Flat ($ lat$) and restores a musical note to its original pitch?
- A) The Natural sign ($
atural$)
- B) The Double Sharp sign
- C) The Fermata pause sign
- D) The Staccato dot
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A Sharp raises pitch by a semitone, a Flat lowers pitch by a semitone, and a Natural restores the original pitch.

[Page 15]
Week 8: Time Signatures, Bar Lines, and Simple Time ($ rac{2}{4},  rac{3}{4},  rac{4}{4}$)
A Time Signature consists of two figures placed one above the other at the beginning of a piece of music right after the clef and key signature. The top figure indicates how many beats are in each bar (measure); the bottom figure indicates the type of note that receives one beat ($2 = 	ext{minim}$, $4 = 	ext{crotchet}$, $8 = 	ext{quaver}$).
Common Time ($C$) represents $\frac{4}{4}$ time ($4$ crotchet beats per bar); Alla Breve (Cut Common Time) represents $\frac{2}{2}$ time ($2$ minim beats per bar).

15. In the time signature $\frac{3}{4}$, what do the upper figure $3$ and the lower figure $4$ specify respectively?
- A) There are $3$ beats in every bar, and each beat has the value of a quarter note (crotchet)
- B) There are $4$ beats in every bar, and each beat has the value of $3$ minims
- C) The music must be played $3$ times faster than $4$ seconds
- D) Only $3$ instruments may play on the $4\text{th}$ line of the staff
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: In $\frac{3}{4}$ (simple triple time), the numerator $3$ means $3$ beats per bar and the denominator $4$ means a quarter note (crotchet) gets $1$ beat.

16. Which vertical line on the musical staff marks the end of a complete composition or a major section?
- A) Double bar line (a thin line followed by a thick vertical line)
- B) Single bar line
- C) Ledger line
- D) Tie curve
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Single bar lines divide music into equal measures, whereas a double bar line (thin-thick) marks the end of a piece.

[Page 18]
Week 9: Classification of African and Western Musical Instruments, the Descant Recorder, and the Keyboard
African traditional musical instruments (Curt Sachs & Erich von Hornbostel classification) are grouped into four classes based on how sound is produced:
1. Idiophones (self-sounding bodies that vibrate without membranes or strings when struck/shaken, e.g., gong/ogene, sekere, xylophone, thumb piano/mbira, woodblock, rattle).
2. Membranophones (sound produced by a stretched animal skin/membrane, e.g., dundun talking drum, bata, omele, igba, tambourine, timpani).
3. Chordophones (sound produced by vibrating stretched strings, e.g., goje, molo, une, kora, violin, guitar, harp).
4. Aerophones (sound produced by a vibrating column of air blown into a tube, e.g., kakaki, algaita,oja flute, horn, trumpet, recorder, clarinet).
Western orchestral instruments are grouped into Strings, Woodwind, Brass, and Percussion.

17. Under the Sachs-Hornbostel classification of African musical instruments, into which categories do the "Ogene (metal gong) / Sekere", "Dundun (talking drum)", "Goje (one-string fiddle)", and "Kakaki (long royal trumpet)" belong respectively?
- A) Idiophone, Membranophone, Chordophone, and Aerophone
- B) Membranophone, Idiophone, Aerophone, and Chordophone
- C) Chordophone, Aerophone, Idiophone, and Membranophone
- D) Aerophone, Chordophone, Membranophone, and Idiophone
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Ogene/Sekere are idiophones (self-sounding body), Dundun is a membranophone (stretched animal skin), Goje is a chordophone (string), and Kakaki is an aerophone (blown air column).

18. On a standard piano or organ keyboard, how are the black keys (sharps and flats) visually arranged across each octave, and where is the note "C" located?
- A) Alternating groups of two black keys and three black keys; the note C is the white key immediately to the left of each group of two black keys
- B) Alternating groups of four black keys and five black keys; the note C is between the middle black keys
- C) Continuous pairs of black keys after every white key; the note C is to the right of three black keys
- D) Three black keys followed by one black key; the note C is a black key
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Black keys are arranged in alternating groups of $2$ and $3$; every white key immediately to the left of the group of $2$ black keys is C, and to the left of the group of $3$ black keys is F.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 1: Introduction to Music — Definition, Origin, and Natural & Human Sources of Musical Sound
weeks.lessonTitle: Introduction to Music — Definition, Origin, and Natural & Human Sources of Musical Sound
weeks.content:
Music is the art and science of combining vocal or instrumental sounds in a pleasing, organized, and expressive manner using rhythm, melody, and harmony.
The word "Music" is derived from the Greek word "Mousike" (the art of the Nine Muses, goddesses of arts and sciences in Greek mythology). Sources of musical sound include natural sources (birdsong, wind, ocean waves, thunder, human voice) and man-made musical instruments.

1. From which ancient language and mythological root is the English word "Music" derived?
- A) The Greek word "Mousike", referring to the art of the Nine Muses
- B) The Latin word "Sonare", referring to Roman military trumpets
- C) The Hebrew word "Selah", referring to temple cymbals
- D) The Sanskrit word "Raga", referring to seasonal rain chants
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: "Music" originates from the Greek "Mousike", meaning the art presided over by the Muses in Greek mythology.

2. What is the fundamental acoustic difference between "Musical Sound" and "Noise"?
- A) Musical sound is produced by regular, periodic vibrations with definite pitch, whereas noise is produced by irregular, non-periodic vibrations displeasing to the ear
- B) Musical sound travels only through vacuum, whereas noise travels only through solid metals
- C) Musical sound has zero frequency, whereas noise has a fixed harmonic overtone series
- D) Musical sound can only be produced by electronic synthesizers, whereas noise is produced by human voices
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Regular periodic vibrations produce musical tone with definite pitch, while irregular vibrations produce noise.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 2: Characteristics (Properties) of Musical Sound and Elements of Music
weeks.lessonTitle: Characteristics (Properties) of Musical Sound and Elements of Music
weeks.content:
Every musical sound possesses four fundamental physical properties: Pitch (height or depth of a sound determined by the frequency of vibration in Hertz), Intensity/Loudness (degree of softness or loudness determined by the amplitude of vibration), Timbre/Quality/Tone Colour (the characteristic quality that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another playing the same pitch, determined by harmonics/overtones), and Duration (length of time a musical sound or silence lasts).
Core elements of music include Rhythm, Melody, Harmony, Dynamics (piano $p$ = soft, forte $f$ = loud, crescendo = gradually louder, diminuendo/decrescendo = gradually softer), Tempo (speed of music: Largo, Adagio, Andante, Moderato, Allegro, Presto), Texture (Monophonic, Homophonic, Polyphonic), and Form (Binary AB, Ternary ABA, Rondo ABACA).

3. If a flute and a violin both play the exact same note Middle C at the exact same loudness for two seconds, which property of musical sound enables a listener to distinguish the flute from the violin?
- A) Timbre (Tone quality or tone colour)
- B) Pitch (Frequency of vibration)
- C) Intensity (Amplitude of vibration)
- D) Duration (Length of note value)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Timbre (tone colour) depends on the harmonic overtones of the instrument and distinguishes different instruments playing the same pitch and loudness.

4. Which physical factor directly determines the Pitch of a musical note?
- A) The frequency (speed) of vibrations per second of the sounding body
- B) The distance between the audience and the concert stage
- C) The colour of the wood used to polish the instrument case
- D) The number of bar lines drawn on the manuscript paper
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Faster vibrations (higher frequency) produce a higher pitch, while slower vibrations (lower frequency) produce a lower pitch.

5. In musical dynamics and tempo terminology, what do the Italian terms "Crescendo" and "Allegro" mean respectively?
- A) Crescendo means gradually getting louder; Allegro means fast, lively, and bright tempo
- B) Crescendo means gradually getting softer; Allegro means very slow and solemn tempo
- C) Crescendo means sudden silence; Allegro means repeating from the beginning
- D) Crescendo means detached staccato notes; Allegro means dying away
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Crescendo ($<$) means gradually becoming louder, and Allegro indicates a fast, lively tempo.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 3: Uses and Impact of Music in Human Society and Nigerian Ceremonies
weeks.lessonTitle: Uses and Impact of Music in Human Society and Nigerian Ceremonies
weeks.content:
Music plays vital roles in society: religious worship and liturgy, royal court ceremonies, lullabies (cradle songs to soothe babies to sleep), work songs (to coordinate manual labour and relieve fatigue), war/military martial songs, healing/therapy, education, entertainment, and commercial advertisement/jingles.

6. What type of traditional vocal music is sung softly by mothers or caregivers with gentle rocking rhythms to soothe an infant to sleep?
- A) Lullaby (cradle song)
- B) Dirge (funeral lament)
- C) Panegyric (royal praise chant)
- D) Martial anthem (war song)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A lullaby is a soothing cradle song sung to calm children and help them fall asleep, whereas a dirge is sung at funerals to mourn the dead.

7. Which type of song is performed at a funeral or memorial service to mourn the dead and express grief?
- A) Dirge (Elegy / Lament)
- B) Epithalamium (wedding song)
- C) Carol (festive nativity song)
- D) Serenade (evening courtship song)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A dirge is a somber funeral song lamenting the deceased.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 4: Musical Notation — Tonic Solfa Notation and Staff (Stave) Notation
weeks.lessonTitle: Musical Notation — Tonic Solfa Notation and Staff (Stave) Notation
weeks.content:
Musical notation is the system of writing down music using visual symbols so that pitch and rhythm can be read and performed.
Tonic Solfa Notation (developed by Sarah Glover and perfected by Rev. John Curwen) uses seven syllabic note names: doh ($d$), ray ($r$), me ($m$), fah ($f$), soh ($s$), lah ($l$), te ($t$).
Staff (Stave) Notation uses five parallel horizontal lines and four equal spaces counted strictly from the BOTTOM to the TOP (Line 1 is the lowest line; Line 5 is the topmost line).

8. Who perfected the Tonic Solfa notation system ($d, r, m, f, s, l, t$) from Sarah Glover's earlier Norwich sol-fa method in the nineteenth century?
- A) Rev. John Curwen
- B) Guido d'Arezzo
- C) Johann Sebastian Bach
- D) Fela Sowande
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Rev. John Curwen refined and popularized the Tonic Solfa system in England in the 1840s based on Sarah Glover's work.

9. How are the five parallel horizontal lines and four spaces of a standard musical Staff (Stave) numbered?
- A) From the bottom upward (the lowest line is Line 1 and the highest line is Line 5)
- B) From the top downward (the highest line is Line 1 and the lowest line is Line 5)
- C) From the middle line outward in both directions
- D) Randomly depending on the tempo of the song
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Staff lines and spaces are always counted from bottom (1st line/space) to top (5th line/4th space).

1. Idiophones (self-sounding bodies that vibrate without membranes or strings when struck/shaken, e.g., gong/ogene, sekere, xylophone, thumb piano/mbira, woodblock, rattle).
2. Membranophones (sound produced by a stretched animal skin/membrane, e.g., dundun talking drum, bata, omele, igba, tambourine, timpani).
3. Chordophones (sound produced by vibrating stretched strings, e.g., goje, molo, une, kora, violin, guitar, harp).
4. Aerophones (sound produced by a vibrating column of air blown into a tube, e.g., kakaki, algaita,oja flute, horn, trumpet, recorder, clarinet).
Western orchestral instruments are grouped into Strings, Woodwind, Brass, and Percussion.

17. Under the Sachs-Hornbostel classification of African musical instruments, into which categories do the "Ogene (metal gong) / Sekere", "Dundun (talking drum)", "Goje (one-string fiddle)", and "Kakaki (long royal trumpet)" belong respectively?
- A) Idiophone, Membranophone, Chordophone, and Aerophone
- B) Membranophone, Idiophone, Aerophone, and Chordophone
- C) Chordophone, Aerophone, Idiophone, and Membranophone
- D) Aerophone, Chordophone, Membranophone, and Idiophone
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Ogene/Sekere are idiophones (self-sounding body), Dundun is a membranophone (stretched animal skin), Goje is a chordophone (string), and Kakaki is an aerophone (blown air column).

18. On a standard piano or organ keyboard, how are the black keys (sharps and flats) visually arranged across each octave, and where is the note "C" located?
- A) Alternating groups of two black keys and three black keys; the note C is the white key immediately to the left of each group of two black keys
- B) Alternating groups of four black keys and five black keys; the note C is between the middle black keys
- C) Continuous pairs of black keys after every white key; the note C is to the right of three black keys
- D) Three black keys followed by one black key; the note C is a black key
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Black keys are arranged in alternating groups of $2$ and $3$; every white key immediately to the left of the group of $2$ black keys is C, and to the left of the group of $3$ black keys is F.

passages.sectionHeading: Week 1: Introduction to Music — Definition, Origin, and Natural & Human Sources of Musical Sound
passages.lessonTitle: Introduction to Music — Definition, Origin, and Natural & Human Sources of Musical Sound
passages.content:
1. From which ancient language and mythological root is the English word "Music" derived? A) The Greek word "Mousike", referring to the art of the Nine Muses B) The Latin word "Sonare", referring to Roman military trumpets C) The Hebrew word "Selah", referring to temple cymbals D) The Sanskrit word "Raga", referring to seasonal rain chants
2. What is the fundamental acoustic difference between "Musical Sound" and "Noise"? A) Musical sound is produced by regular, periodic vibrations with definite pitch, whereas noise is produced by irregular, non-periodic vibrations displeasing to the ear B) Musical sound travels only through vacuum, whereas noise travels only through solid metals C) Musical sound has zero frequency, whereas noise has a fixed harmonic overtone series D) Musical sound can only be produced by electronic synthesizers, whereas noise is produced by human voices
keyFacts: @@MCQ@@{"questionNumber":1,"stem":"From which ancient language and mythological root is the English word \"Music\" derived?","options":["The Greek word \"Mousike\", referring to the art of the Nine Muses","The Latin word \"Sonare\", referring to Roman military trumpets","The Hebrew word \"Selah\", referring to temple cymbals","The Sanskrit word \"Raga\", referring to seasonal rain chants"],"correctOptionId":"A","explanation":"\"Music\" originates from the Greek \"Mousike\", meaning the art presided over by the Muses in Greek mythology."}

@@MCQ@@{"questionNumber":2,"stem":"What is the fundamental acoustic difference between \"Musical Sound\" and \"Noise\"?","options":["Musical sound is produced by regular, periodic vibrations with definite pitch, whereas noise is produced by irregular, non-periodic vibrations displeasing to the ear","Musical sound travels only through vacuum, whereas noise travels only through solid metals","Musical sound has zero frequency, whereas noise has a fixed harmonic overtone series","Musical sound can only be produced by electronic synthesizers, whereas noise is produced by human voices"],"correctOptionId":"A","explanation":"Regular periodic vibrations produce musical tone with definite pitch, while irregular vibrations produce noise."}

passages.content:
3. If a flute and a violin both play the exact same note Middle C at the exact same loudness for two seconds, which property of musical sound enables a listener to distinguish the flute from the violin? A) Timbre (Tone quality or tone colour) B) Pitch (Frequency of vibration) C) Intensity (Amplitude of vibration) D) Duration (Length of note value)
4. Which physical factor directly determines the Pitch of a musical note? A) The frequency (speed) of vibrations per second of the sounding body B) The distance between the audience and the concert stage C) The colour of the wood used to polish the instrument case D) The number of bar lines drawn on the manuscript paper
5. In musical dynamics and tempo terminology, what do the Italian terms "Crescendo" and "Allegro" mean respectively? A) Crescendo means gradually getting louder; Allegro means fast, lively, and bright tempo B) Crescendo means gradually getting softer; Allegro means very slow and solemn tempo C) Crescendo means sudden silence; Allegro means repeating from the beginning D) Crescendo means detached staccato notes; Allegro means dying away

@@MCQ@@{"questionNumber":4,"stem":"Which physical factor directly determines the Pitch of a musical note?","options":["The frequency (speed) of vibrations per second of the sounding body","The distance between the audience and the concert stage","The colour of the wood used to polish the instrument case","The number of bar lines drawn on the manuscript paper"],"correctOptionId":"A","explanation":"Faster vibrations (higher frequency) produce a higher pitch, while slower vibrations (lower frequency) produce a lower pitch."}

@@MCQ@@{"questionNumber":5,"stem":"In musical dynamics and tempo terminology, what do the Italian terms \"Crescendo\" and \"Allegro\" mean respectively?","options":["Crescendo means gradually getting louder; Allegro means fast, lively, and bright tempo","Crescendo means gradually getting softer; Allegro means very slow and solemn tempo","Crescendo means sudden silence; Allegro means repeating from the beginning","Crescendo means detached staccato notes; Allegro means dying away"],"correctOptionId":"A","explanation":"Crescendo ($<$) means gradually becoming louder, and Allegro indicates a fast, lively tempo."}

10. Why is the Treble Clef also known as the "G Clef", and why is the Bass Clef also known as the "F Clef"? A) The Treble Clef's inner loop curls around the 2nd line fixing it as note G, while the Bass Clef's two dots sit above and below the 4th line fixing it as note F B) The Treble Clef was invented in Germany, while the Bass Clef was invented in France C) The Treble Clef is used only for guitars, while the Bass Clef is used only for flutes D) The Treble Clef has 7 lines, while the Bass Clef has 6 lines

documents.title: JSS 1 Digital Technology — St. Francis Catholic Secondary School First Term (Weeks 1–10)
documents.subject: Digital Technology
documents.description: St. Francis Catholic Secondary School Lagos JSS 1 Digital Technologies First Term Note covering Introduction to Digital Technologies, History & Generations of Computers (1st–5th), Classification of Computers, Computer System Components (Hardware, Software, Peopleware), CPU Architecture, and Word Processing with Microsoft Word (Weeks 1–10).
documents.rawText:
[Page 1]
Week 1: Introduction to Digital Technologies — Meaning, Data vs Information, and Early Counting Devices
Digital technology refers to electronic tools, systems, devices, and resources that generate, store, process, and transmit data in binary digital form ($0\text{s}$ and $1\text{s}$).
Data consists of raw, unorganized facts, figures, and symbols (such as raw test scores), whereas Information is processed, organized, and meaningful data useful for decision-making (such as a class average and grade sheet).
Before modern computers, early humans used fingers, toes, pebbles, tally sticks, cowries, and the Abacus (invented in ancient China/Babylon for arithmetic place-value counting).

1. What is the fundamental distinction between "Data" and "Information" in computing?
- A) Data consists of raw, unprocessed facts and figures, whereas Information is data that has been processed, organized, and structured to be meaningful
- B) Data is the final printed report from a printer, whereas Information is the unformatted electrical voltage in a cable
- C) Data can only be stored on paper, whereas Information cannot be stored on a hard drive
- D) Data is always accurate and summarized, whereas Information is random and unverified
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Data is raw input fed into the computer; after processing by the CPU, it becomes meaningful output called Information.

2. Which early manual calculating device consists of a wooden frame holding parallel rods with sliding beads divided into upper and lower decks?
- A) The Abacus
- B) Napier's Bones
- C) The Jacquard Loom
- D) Herman Hollerith's Tabulating Machine
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The Abacus is the ancient bead-and-rod counting frame used for addition and subtraction.

[Page 3]
Week 2: Historical Development of Computers — Mechanical and Electro-Mechanical Counting Devices
1. John Napier ($1617$) invented Napier's Bones (ivory/wooden rods used for multiplication and division) and logarithms.
2. William Oughtred ($1622$) invented the Slide Rule based on logarithms.
3. Blaise Pascal ($1642$) invented the Pascaline (the first mechanical adding machine using toothed gear wheels to help his tax-collector father).
4. Gottfried Wilhelm von Leibniz ($1671$) invented the Stepped Reckoner (which could add, subtract, multiply, divide, and extract square roots).
5. Joseph Marie Jacquard ($1801$) used punched cards to control textile weaving patterns on the Jacquard Loom.
6. Charles Babbage ($1822 / 1833$), known as the "Father of the Computer", designed the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine (which featured a Mill/ALU, Store/Memory, input, and output), assisted by Lady Ada Lovelace (the world's first computer programmer).
7. Herman Hollerith ($1890$) built the Electro-Mechanical Punched Card Tabulating Machine used for the $1890$ US Census and founded the company that later became IBM.

3. Why is Charles Babbage universally recognized as the "Father of the Modern Computer", and who is recognized as the "First Computer Programmer"?
- A) Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine containing the core architecture of modern computers (input, store/memory, mill/processor, output), and Lady Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm for it
- B) Charles Babbage invented the silicon microchip in 1971, and Bill Gates wrote the first punched card for the 1890 census
- C) Charles Babbage built the wooden Abacus, and Blaise Pascal wrote the Microsoft Windows operating system
- D) Charles Babbage invented the vacuum tube, and Herman Hollerith invented the slide rule
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Babbage's Analytical Engine ($1833$) established the logical blueprint of programmable computers, and Lady Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm for it.

4. Which nineteenth-century pioneer invented the electro-mechanical punched card tabulating machine that processed the $1890$ United States Census in record time?
- A) Herman Hollerith
- B) Gottfried Wilhelm von Leibniz
- C) John Napier
- D) William Oughtred
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Herman Hollerith's electro-mechanical punched card tabulator processed the $1890$ US Census and led to the formation of IBM.

[Page 6]
Week 3: Generations of Electronic Computers (First to Fifth Generation)
Electronic computers evolved through five technological generations based on their core switching circuitry:
- First Generation ($1940	ext{–}1956$): Vacuum Tubes (Thermionic Valves); magnetic drums for memory; machine language ($0	ext{s}$ and $1	ext{s}$); huge size, generated intense heat, consumed massive electricity (e.g., ENIAC, EDVAC, UNIVAC I).
- Second Generation ($1956	ext{–}1963$): Transistors (invented at Bell Labs); magnetic core memory; assembly and early high-level languages (FORTRAN, COBOL); smaller, faster, and cooler than vacuum tubes (e.g., IBM 1401, ATLAS).
- Third Generation ($1964	ext{–}1971$): Integrated Circuits (ICs — silicon chips containing many transistors); keyboards and monitors introduced instead of punched cards; operating systems and multiprogramming (e.g., IBM System/360).
- Fourth Generation ($1971	ext{–Present}$): Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Microprocessors (entire CPU on a single silicon chip, starting with Intel 4004); Personal Computers (PCs), GUIs, LAN/Internet (e.g., IBM PC, Apple Macintosh).
- Fifth Generation (Present & Beyond): Artificial Intelligence (AI), Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI), parallel processing, natural language recognition, robotics, and expert systems.

5. Which sequence correctly matches the First, Second, Third, and Fourth Generations of computers with their defining hardware switching technology?
- A) 1st: Vacuum Tubes $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Transistors $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Integrated Circuits (ICs) $\rightarrow$ 4th: VLSI Microprocessors
- B) 1st: Transistors $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Vacuum Tubes $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Microprocessors $\rightarrow$ 4th: Abacus beads
- C) 1st: Integrated Circuits $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Microprocessors $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Transistors $\rightarrow$ 4th: Vacuum Tubes
- D) 1st: Silicon Chips $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Punched Cards $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Magnetic Drums $\rightarrow$ 4th: Relay Switches
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Computer generations progressed from Vacuum Tubes (1st) to Transistors (2nd), Integrated Circuits (3rd), VLSI Microprocessors (4th), and AI/ULSI (5th).

6. Why did First Generation computers (such as ENIAC and UNIVAC I) require massive air-conditioning systems and frequent component replacements?
- A) They relied on thousands of fragile glass Vacuum Tubes (thermionic valves) that generated enormous heat and burned out frequently
- B) They used solar-powered microprocessors that overheated in sunlight
- C) They had liquid mercury keyboards that boiled at room temperature
- D) They ran on steam engines connected to mechanical looms
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: First-generation vacuum tubes consumed huge amounts of electricity and radiated intense heat.

[Page 9]
Week 4: Classification of Computers by Type (Signal), Size, and Purpose
1. By Type (Nature of Data/Signal Handled):
   - Digital Computers: Process discrete binary data ($0$ and $1$) by counting (e.g., laptops, calculators, desktop PCs).
   - Analog Computers: Measure continuous physical quantities such as temperature, pressure, voltage, or speed (e.g., thermometer, speedometer, aneroid barometer, fuel dispenser gauge).
   - Hybrid Computers: Combine both analog measurement and digital processing (e.g., hospital ICU ECG patient monitors, automated petrol station pumps, weather radar systems).
2. By Size and Processing Capacity (from largest/fastest to smallest):
   - Supercomputers (fastest, used for weather forecasting, nuclear simulations, space research) $\rightarrow$ Mainframe Computers (support hundreds/thousands of simultaneous users in banks and airlines) $\rightarrow$ Minicomputers (mid-range servers) $\rightarrow$ Microcomputers (Personal Computers: desktops, laptops, tablets, smartphones).
3. By Purpose: General-Purpose Computers vs Special-Purpose (Dedicated) Computers (e.g., ATM machines, traffic light controllers, aircraft flight-control systems).

7. An Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patient monitor in a hospital measures a patient's continuous analog heartbeat and blood pressure waves and converts them into digital numerical readouts on a screen. How is this computer classified by type?
- A) Hybrid computer
- B) Purely mechanical computer
- C) First-generation vacuum computer
- D) Slide-rule analog calculator
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: A hybrid computer combines analog components (sensing continuous physical signals) with digital components (processing and displaying discrete numerical values).

8. Arrange the four classes of computers by size and processing power in descending order (from the most powerful to the smallest):
- A) Supercomputer $\rightarrow$ Mainframe computer $\rightarrow$ Minicomputer $\rightarrow$ Microcomputer
- B) Mainframe computer $\rightarrow$ Supercomputer $\rightarrow$ Microcomputer $\rightarrow$ Minicomputer
- C) Microcomputer $\rightarrow$ Minicomputer $\rightarrow$ Mainframe computer $\rightarrow$ Supercomputer
- D) Supercomputer $\rightarrow$ Microcomputer $\rightarrow$ Mainframe computer $\rightarrow$ Minicomputer
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Supercomputers are the fastest and most powerful, followed by Mainframes, Minicomputers, and Microcomputers (PCs).

[Page 12]
Week 5: The Computer System — Hardware, Software, and Peopleware (Humanware)
A complete computer system is made up of three interdependent components:
1. Hardware: The physical, tangible parts of the computer that can be seen and touched (System Unit and Peripherals: input, output, and storage devices).
2. Software: The intangible set of programs and instructions that tell the hardware what to do and how to do it. Software is divided into System Software (Operating Systems like Windows, macOS, Linux, Android; utility programs; language translators) and Application Software (Word processors like MS Word, spreadsheets like MS Excel, browsers, games).
3. Peopleware (Humanware/Liveware): The human users and professionals who design, program, operate, and maintain the computer system (system analysts, programmers, network administrators, end-users).

9. Which of the following pairs correctly distinguishes "System Software" from "Application Software"?
- A) Microsoft Windows 11 and Linux are System Software (Operating Systems) that manage hardware resources, whereas Microsoft Word and CorelDRAW are Application Software used for specific user tasks
- B) Microsoft Word is System Software, whereas the BIOS and Windows Operating System are Application Software
- C) Keyboards and monitors are System Software, whereas printers and scanners are Application Software
- D) Computer programmers are System Software, whereas typists are Application Software
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS) are System Software that control the hardware, while MS Word, Excel, and CorelDRAW are Application Software.

[Page 14]
Week 6: Computer Hardware — Input Devices, Output Devices, the Central Processing Unit (CPU), and Primary/Secondary Memory
- Input Devices convert human-readable data into binary signals for the CPU: Keyboard, Mouse, Scanner, Microphone, Joystick, Light pen, Webcam, Barcode reader, Optical Mark Reader (OMR — used for grading multiple-choice shading sheets).
- The Central Processing Unit (CPU), the "brain of the computer", consists of three internal units:
  1. Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU): Performs all arithmetic calculations ($+, -, \times, \div$) and logical comparisons ($<, >, =, \text{AND}, \text{OR}, \text{NOT}$).
  2. Control Unit (CU): Directs, coordinates, and supervises the flow of data and instructions across the entire computer system (fetch-decode-execute cycle).
  3. Registers: High-speed temporary storage locations inside the CPU.
- Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory — volatile read/write working memory that loses its contents when power is switched off) and ROM (Read-Only Memory — non-volatile permanent memory storing boot-up BIOS instructions).
- Output Devices convert processed binary information into human-readable form: Monitor/VDU (softcopy output), Printer and Plotter (hardcopy output), Speaker, and Projector.

10. Which internal component of the Central Processing Unit (CPU) is specifically responsible for executing logical comparisons (such as testing whether Score $\ge 50$) and arithmetic operations?
- A) Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU)
- B) Control Unit (CU)
- C) Read-Only Memory (ROM)
- D) Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations and logical comparisons, while the Control Unit directs and coordinates operations.

11. What is the critical difference between RAM (Random Access Memory) and ROM (Read-Only Memory)?
- A) RAM is volatile temporary working memory whose contents are lost when power is turned off, whereas ROM is non-volatile permanent memory that retains start-up firmware even without power
- B) RAM is non-volatile permanent optical storage, whereas ROM erases itself every time a key is pressed
- C) RAM is an external output device, whereas ROM is an input pointing device
- D) RAM stores only audio files, whereas ROM stores only printed paper copies
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: RAM is volatile read/write memory used for currently running programs, whereas ROM is non-volatile memory storing essential boot instructions (BIOS).

12. Which input device is specifically used by examination bodies (such as WAEC, NECO, and JAMB) to automatically scan and grade shaded pencil circles on multiple-choice answer sheets?
- A) Optical Mark Reader (OMR)
- B) Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR) reader
- C) Plotter
- D) Trackball
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: OMR detects the presence or absence of shaded pencil marks on objective test forms, whereas MICR reads magnetic ink characters at the bottom of bank cheques.

[Page 17]
Week 8: Word Processing I — Meaning, Examples of Word Processors, and Features of the Microsoft Word Interface
Word Processing is the use of specialized application software (a word processor) to create, edit, format, spell-check, save, and print text documents such as letters, reports, memos, and exam papers.
Examples of Word Processors include Microsoft Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice Writer, Apple Pages, Corel WordPerfect, and WordPad.
Key elements of the Microsoft Word window include: Title Bar (displays document name and program name, plus Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close buttons), Quick Access Toolbar (Save, Undo, Redo), Ribbon Tabs (File, Home, Insert, Design, Layout, References, Review, View), Ruler, Document Workspace (Insertion Point / Cursor), Scroll Bars, and Status Bar (displays page number, word count, and zoom slider).

13. In the Microsoft Word interface, which bar at the very top of the window displays the filename of the currently active document (e.g., "Assignment1.docx - Word") and which bar at the bottom displays the live Page Count and Word Count?
- A) Title Bar (at the top) and Status Bar (at the bottom)
- B) Status Bar (at the top) and Scroll Bar (at the bottom)
- C) Taskbar (at the top) and Formula Bar (at the bottom)
- D) Address Bar (at the top) and Navigation Pane (at the bottom)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The Title Bar at the top shows the document title and application name, while the Status Bar at the bottom shows the page number, word count, and zoom controls.

14. Which of the following software packages is a Spreadsheet application rather than a Word Processor?
- A) Microsoft Excel
- B) Microsoft Word
- C) Corel WordPerfect
- D) LibreOffice Writer
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet program for numerical rows/columns and formulas, whereas MS Word, WordPerfect, and LibreOffice Writer are word processors.

[Page 20]
Week 9: Word Processing II — Creating, Entering Text, Editing, Saving, and Retrieving Documents
Editing a document involves correcting mistakes, inserting, deleting, copying, moving (cutting and pasting), and finding/replacing text.
- The Backspace key deletes the character immediately to the LEFT of the blinking cursor (insertion point), whereas the Delete key deletes the character immediately to the RIGHT of the blinking cursor.
- "Save As" is used the first time a document is saved to specify its filename, file format (.docx or .pdf), and storage folder (or to save a copy under a new name), whereas "Save" (Ctrl + S) updates changes to an already named file.

15. When editing text in Microsoft Word, what is the exact difference between pressing the "Backspace" key and pressing the "Delete" key?
- A) Backspace erases one character to the left of the blinking insertion point, whereas Delete erases one character to the right of the blinking insertion point
- B) Backspace erases the entire paragraph below the cursor, whereas Delete saves the document
- C) Backspace erases characters to the right of the cursor, whereas Delete erases characters to the left
- D) Backspace capitalizes selected letters, whereas Delete underlines them
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Backspace removes characters to the left of the cursor; Delete removes characters to the right of the cursor (or any highlighted selection).

16. What is the difference between the "Copy and Paste" (Ctrl + C then Ctrl + V) operation and the "Cut and Paste" (Ctrl + X then Ctrl + V) operation?
- A) Copy and Paste duplicates the selected text at the new location while leaving the original text intact, whereas Cut and Paste removes the text from its original location and moves it to the new location
- B) Copy and Paste deletes the text permanently, whereas Cut and Paste prints the text to a laser printer
- C) Copy and Paste changes the font colour to red, whereas Cut and Paste checks spelling
- D) Both operations erase the entire hard disk
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Copy duplicates text, whereas Cut moves text from its source location to the clipboard for pasting elsewhere.

[Page 22]
Week 10: Word Processing III — Formatting Text, Paragraph Alignment, and Essential Keyboard Shortcuts in Microsoft Word
Formatting changes the visual appearance of text and pages: Font family (Times New Roman, Calibri, Arial), Font size (points), Font style (Bold Ctrl + B, Italic Ctrl + I, Underline Ctrl + U), Superscript ($x^2$), Subscript ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), and Text Alignment:
- Align Left (Ctrl + L): Aligns text flush with the left margin (ragged right).
- Center (Ctrl + E): Centers headings symmetrically between left and right margins.
- Align Right (Ctrl + R): Aligns text flush with the right margin.
- Justify (Ctrl + J): Aligns text evenly along BOTH the left and right margins.
Undo is Ctrl + Z; Redo is Ctrl + Y; Select All is Ctrl + A; Print is Ctrl + P.

17. In Microsoft Word, why is the keyboard shortcut for centering a paragraph Ctrl + E rather than Ctrl + C, and what is the shortcut for "Justify" alignment (even left and right margins)?
- A) Ctrl + C is already reserved for "Copy", so Ctrl + E centers text, while Ctrl + J justifies text evenly on both margins
- B) Ctrl + C closes the computer, while Ctrl + E erases the paragraph
- C) Ctrl + E exports to Excel, while Ctrl + J joins two monitors
- D) Ctrl + R centers text, while Ctrl + L justifies text
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Ctrl + C copies selected content to the clipboard; Ctrl + E centers text; Ctrl + L left-aligns; Ctrl + R right-aligns; and Ctrl + J justifies text across both margins.

18. A student accidentally deletes a whole paragraph while typing an essay in Microsoft Word. Which keyboard shortcut immediately reverses (undoes) that last action and restores the paragraph?
- A) Ctrl + Z (Undo)
- B) Ctrl + S (Save)
- C) Ctrl + P (Print)
- D) Ctrl + F (Find)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Ctrl + Z executes the Undo command to reverse the most recent action, whereas Ctrl + Y executes Redo.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 1: Introduction to Digital Technologies — Meaning, Data vs Information, and Early Counting Devices
weeks.lessonTitle: Introduction to Digital Technologies — Meaning, Data vs Information, and Early Counting Devices
weeks.content:
Digital technology refers to electronic tools, systems, devices, and resources that generate, store, process, and transmit data in binary digital form ($0\text{s}$ and $1\text{s}$).
Data consists of raw, unorganized facts, figures, and symbols (such as raw test scores), whereas Information is processed, organized, and meaningful data useful for decision-making (such as a class average and grade sheet).
Before modern computers, early humans used fingers, toes, pebbles, tally sticks, cowries, and the Abacus (invented in ancient China/Babylon for arithmetic place-value counting).

1. What is the fundamental distinction between "Data" and "Information" in computing?
- A) Data consists of raw, unprocessed facts and figures, whereas Information is data that has been processed, organized, and structured to be meaningful
- B) Data is the final printed report from a printer, whereas Information is the unformatted electrical voltage in a cable
- C) Data can only be stored on paper, whereas Information cannot be stored on a hard drive
- D) Data is always accurate and summarized, whereas Information is random and unverified
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Data is raw input fed into the computer; after processing by the CPU, it becomes meaningful output called Information.

2. Which early manual calculating device consists of a wooden frame holding parallel rods with sliding beads divided into upper and lower decks?
- A) The Abacus
- B) Napier's Bones
- C) The Jacquard Loom
- D) Herman Hollerith's Tabulating Machine
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The Abacus is the ancient bead-and-rod counting frame used for addition and subtraction.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 2: Historical Development of Computers — Mechanical and Electro-Mechanical Counting Devices
weeks.lessonTitle: Historical Development of Computers — Mechanical and Electro-Mechanical Counting Devices
weeks.content:
1. John Napier ($1617$) invented Napier's Bones (ivory/wooden rods used for multiplication and division) and logarithms.
2. William Oughtred ($1622$) invented the Slide Rule based on logarithms.
3. Blaise Pascal ($1642$) invented the Pascaline (the first mechanical adding machine using toothed gear wheels to help his tax-collector father).
4. Gottfried Wilhelm von Leibniz ($1671$) invented the Stepped Reckoner (which could add, subtract, multiply, divide, and extract square roots).
5. Joseph Marie Jacquard ($1801$) used punched cards to control textile weaving patterns on the Jacquard Loom.
6. Charles Babbage ($1822 / 1833$), known as the "Father of the Computer", designed the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine (which featured a Mill/ALU, Store/Memory, input, and output), assisted by Lady Ada Lovelace (the world's first computer programmer).
7. Herman Hollerith ($1890$) built the Electro-Mechanical Punched Card Tabulating Machine used for the $1890$ US Census and founded the company that later became IBM.

3. Why is Charles Babbage universally recognized as the "Father of the Modern Computer", and who is recognized as the "First Computer Programmer"?
- A) Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine containing the core architecture of modern computers (input, store/memory, mill/processor, output), and Lady Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm for it
- B) Charles Babbage invented the silicon microchip in 1971, and Bill Gates wrote the first punched card for the 1890 census
- C) Charles Babbage built the wooden Abacus, and Blaise Pascal wrote the Microsoft Windows operating system
- D) Charles Babbage invented the vacuum tube, and Herman Hollerith invented the slide rule
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Babbage's Analytical Engine ($1833$) established the logical blueprint of programmable computers, and Lady Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm for it.

4. Which nineteenth-century pioneer invented the electro-mechanical punched card tabulating machine that processed the $1890$ United States Census in record time?
- A) Herman Hollerith
- B) Gottfried Wilhelm von Leibniz
- C) John Napier
- D) William Oughtred
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Herman Hollerith's electro-mechanical punched card tabulator processed the $1890$ US Census and led to the formation of IBM.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 3: Generations of Electronic Computers (First to Fifth Generation)
weeks.lessonTitle: Generations of Electronic Computers (First to Fifth Generation)
weeks.content:
Electronic computers evolved through five technological generations based on their core switching circuitry:
- First Generation ($1940	ext{–}1956$): Vacuum Tubes (Thermionic Valves); magnetic drums for memory; machine language ($0	ext{s}$ and $1	ext{s}$); huge size, generated intense heat, consumed massive electricity (e.g., ENIAC, EDVAC, UNIVAC I).
- Second Generation ($1956	ext{–}1963$): Transistors (invented at Bell Labs); magnetic core memory; assembly and early high-level languages (FORTRAN, COBOL); smaller, faster, and cooler than vacuum tubes (e.g., IBM 1401, ATLAS).
- Third Generation ($1964	ext{–}1971$): Integrated Circuits (ICs — silicon chips containing many transistors); keyboards and monitors introduced instead of punched cards; operating systems and multiprogramming (e.g., IBM System/360).
- Fourth Generation ($1971	ext{–Present}$): Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Microprocessors (entire CPU on a single silicon chip, starting with Intel 4004); Personal Computers (PCs), GUIs, LAN/Internet (e.g., IBM PC, Apple Macintosh).
- Fifth Generation (Present & Beyond): Artificial Intelligence (AI), Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI), parallel processing, natural language recognition, robotics, and expert systems.

5. Which sequence correctly matches the First, Second, Third, and Fourth Generations of computers with their defining hardware switching technology?
- A) 1st: Vacuum Tubes $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Transistors $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Integrated Circuits (ICs) $\rightarrow$ 4th: VLSI Microprocessors
- B) 1st: Transistors $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Vacuum Tubes $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Microprocessors $\rightarrow$ 4th: Abacus beads
- C) 1st: Integrated Circuits $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Microprocessors $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Transistors $\rightarrow$ 4th: Vacuum Tubes
- D) 1st: Silicon Chips $\rightarrow$ 2nd: Punched Cards $\rightarrow$ 3rd: Magnetic Drums $\rightarrow$ 4th: Relay Switches
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Computer generations progressed from Vacuum Tubes (1st) to Transistors (2nd), Integrated Circuits (3rd), VLSI Microprocessors (4th), and AI/ULSI (5th).

6. Why did First Generation computers (such as ENIAC and UNIVAC I) require massive air-conditioning systems and frequent component replacements?
- A) They relied on thousands of fragile glass Vacuum Tubes (thermionic valves) that generated enormous heat and burned out frequently
- B) They used solar-powered microprocessors that overheated in sunlight
- C) They had liquid mercury keyboards that boiled at room temperature
- D) They ran on steam engines connected to mechanical looms
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: First-generation vacuum tubes consumed huge amounts of electricity and radiated intense heat.

Explanation: Backspace removes characters to the left of the cursor; Delete removes characters to the right of the cursor (or any highlighted selection).

16. What is the difference between the "Copy and Paste" (Ctrl + C then Ctrl + V) operation and the "Cut and Paste" (Ctrl + X then Ctrl + V) operation?
- A) Copy and Paste duplicates the selected text at the new location while leaving the original text intact, whereas Cut and Paste removes the text from its original location and moves it to the new location
- B) Copy and Paste deletes the text permanently, whereas Cut and Paste prints the text to a laser printer
- C) Copy and Paste changes the font colour to red, whereas Cut and Paste checks spelling
- D) Both operations erase the entire hard disk
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Copy duplicates text, whereas Cut moves text from its source location to the clipboard for pasting elsewhere.

weeks.detectedHeading: Week 10: Word Processing III — Formatting Text, Paragraph Alignment, and Essential Keyboard Shortcuts in Microsoft Word
weeks.lessonTitle: Word Processing III — Formatting Text, Paragraph Alignment, and Essential Keyboard Shortcuts in Microsoft Word
weeks.content:
Formatting changes the visual appearance of text and pages: Font family (Times New Roman, Calibri, Arial), Font size (points), Font style (Bold Ctrl + B, Italic Ctrl + I, Underline Ctrl + U), Superscript ($x^2$), Subscript ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), and Text Alignment:
- Align Left (Ctrl + L): Aligns text flush with the left margin (ragged right).
- Center (Ctrl + E): Centers headings symmetrically between left and right margins.
- Align Right (Ctrl + R): Aligns text flush with the right margin.
- Justify (Ctrl + J): Aligns text evenly along BOTH the left and right margins.
Undo is Ctrl + Z; Redo is Ctrl + Y; Select All is Ctrl + A; Print is Ctrl + P.

17. In Microsoft Word, why is the keyboard shortcut for centering a paragraph Ctrl + E rather than Ctrl + C, and what is the shortcut for "Justify" alignment (even left and right margins)?
- A) Ctrl + C is already reserved for "Copy", so Ctrl + E centers text, while Ctrl + J justifies text evenly on both margins
- B) Ctrl + C closes the computer, while Ctrl + E erases the paragraph
- C) Ctrl + E exports to Excel, while Ctrl + J joins two monitors
- D) Ctrl + R centers text, while Ctrl + L justifies text
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Ctrl + C copies selected content to the clipboard; Ctrl + E centers text; Ctrl + L left-aligns; Ctrl + R right-aligns; and Ctrl + J justifies text across both margins.

18. A student accidentally deletes a whole paragraph while typing an essay in Microsoft Word. Which keyboard shortcut immediately reverses (undoes) that last action and restores the paragraph?
- A) Ctrl + Z (Undo)
- B) Ctrl + S (Save)
- C) Ctrl + P (Print)
- D) Ctrl + F (Find)
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Ctrl + Z executes the Undo command to reverse the most recent action, whereas Ctrl + Y executes Redo.

passages.content:
1. What is the fundamental distinction between "Data" and "Information" in computing? A) Data consists of raw, unprocessed facts and figures, whereas Information is data that has been processed, organized, and structured to be meaningful B) Data is the final printed report from a printer, whereas Information is the unformatted electrical voltage in a cable C) Data can only be stored on paper, whereas Information cannot be stored on a hard drive D) Data is always accurate and summarized, whereas Information is random and unverified
2. Which early manual calculating device consists of a wooden frame holding parallel rods with sliding beads divided into upper and lower decks? A) The Abacus B) Napier's Bones C) The Jacquard Loom D) Herman Hollerith's Tabulating Machine
